To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) both between and within-therapists differences in autonomous and controlled motivation predict outcome, (b) between-therapies differences in relational support (friendlness) predict autonomous motivation, and (c) within-therapist patient differences in perfectionism predict controlled motivation.
both within-therapist and between-therapist differences are important to consider when examining the effects of patient motivation and perceived therapist support on outcomes in psychotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of therapists’ interpersonal behaviors in the process of psychotherapy and their impact on patients’ motivation.
the effects of therapist and patient characteristics on outcome in IPT for depression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more therapists are able to provide a supportive environment, the more their patients will experience autonomy and less control.
both therapists and their patients are important in determining outcome.

both therapist-level and patient within-therapist factors are associated with patient outcome in IPT for depression, and that therapist-level relational support is a predictor of patient-level autonomous motivation, which in turn predicts patient-level outcome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of the interpersonal relationship is a key element of effective treatment.
the interpersonal impact of the therapist is a key element in the process of change in IPT.
therapists who provide relational support are likely to elicit autonomous motivation and thereby improve outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
therapists should be aware of the interpersonal impact they make on their patients and monitor their own interpersonal behavior.
both between- and within-therapists effects are relevant for understanding outcome, and that the SDT constructs of autonomous and controlled motives are important for understanding such effects.
therapists’ interpersonal impact is a crucial determinant of patients’ motivation and outcome.
